The major flaw is control—his command grade translates to just 20 on the tool scale—and he's cooling in ValuCast's rankings as that risk compounds. This is a thin current sample from late June, so volatility in both direction is real, but his ceiling projects as a useful depth arm rather than a rotation piece.

804558_hitter.text: Raudi Rodriguez is a disciplined, high-contact hitter operating well above the strikeout-to-walk balance typical of minor leaguers, built on a .424 OBP and 16.5% BB% that grade 96th and 88th respectively in the ValuCast hitter pool. The projection calls for a second-division regular within one to two years, though recent ranking movement has cooled slightly; this 285-PA sample is fresh and carries moderate confidence in the translation, making the next phase of development critical for determining whether the approach profile can sustain premium value as competition tightens.

804560_hitter.text: Charles Davalan is a contact-first left-handed hitter who works counts and avoids strikeouts at an elite rate, posting an 11.5 K%, well above the 98th percentile, while walking in 13.3% of his plate appearances and building a .392 OBP. The floor is immediate and real—his .171 ISO ranks 65th percentile and projects to just .13 in the majors, making him a pure line-drive hitter with limited impact potential. ValuCast sees him as a bench or platoon bat (85% probability), though the data suggests upside remains untapped at age 22 with 286 PA through A+ ball. The sample is current and clean, but the power profile is the binding constraint on ceiling.

804614_hitter.text: Marco Vargas is a 21-year-old shortstop operating at AA with a low-impact offensive profile: he's whiffing at an unsustainable rate while generating minimal power. His 27.1 K% ranks in the 36th percentile and his .080 ISO in the 13th percentile of the hitter pool, leaving him dependent on a 15.3 BB% (80th percentile) to manufacture any value—and even that elite walk rate hasn't lifted his .331 OBP or .621 OPS into playable territory at the upper minors. The core risk is real power production that hasn't materialized across 118 plate appearances; his bat speed and exit velo would need to demonstrate a marked step forward to suggest this strikeout rate and slugging are temporary. This is a thin current sample at a pivotal level, so confidence in any direction is low.

804619_pitcher.text: John Klein is a mid-rotation depth arm with swing-and-miss feel but durability concerns—strikeout rates play (10.7 K/9 at AAA translates to 9.0 K/9 at MLB), and his 17.4% K-BB% sits 75th percentile, but a 6.53 ERA and 1.35 WHIP in just 41.3 innings reveal he's getting hit when contact is made and missing too many spots (3.9 BB/9). The main risk is raw command consistency and whether his velocity plays in the zone consistently at the highest level. This is a thin current sample with no depth yet—confidence in any full-season read is limited.

804636_pitcher.text: Jonah Tong is a high-strikeout, high-walk right-hander whose K/9 rate sits well above league average when translated to MLB (9.7 versus 8.6), but whose 4.7 BB/9 MLB-equivalent is substantially above average and drives an ERA of 6.3 at AAA. The walk rate is the binding constraint—his K-BB% of 12.9 (MLB-equivalent) trails the MLB average despite elite strikeout stuff, a profile that suggests he'll need significant command work before reliably succeeding at the big-league level. The 50-inning sample is fresh and clear, though modest in size.

804645_hitter.text: Caden Connor is a left-handed hitter whose discipline appears intact but whose raw power production is lagging at the upper minors. Through 199 PA at AAA, he's striking out in the 91st percentile (15.6%) while posting a .12 ISO that ranks only 31st—well below the .15 MLB average the translation projects he'd need. The lack of impact in the box is the real constraint; strikeout rate alone doesn't disqualify prospects, but when paired with power that doesn't match his level, the offensive ceiling narrows to organizational depth rather than prospect leverage.

804817_pitcher.text: Kyson Witherspoon is a right-handed starter with below-average command and strike-to-ball leverage—his K/9 of 9.6 sits at the 49th percentile while his BB/9 of 4.4 places him at the 51st percentile, leaving a K-BB% of just 14% that trails the average starter profile. The walk rate is the immediate problem; at 4.4 BB/9, he's consistently behind in counts and bleeding free baserunners in his 57 innings at A+. ValuCast's projection slots him as a back-end starter with medium risk, though the role probability (49% useful MLB arm, 28% depth/relief) reflects real uncertainty about whether the current velocity and movement can sustain a high-leverage role. This is a fresh full-season sample with no staleness, but the command grade of 40 and dominance grade of 45 suggest the floor may define his path more than the ceiling.

804858_hitter.text: Bryan Rincon is a high-contact, selective hitter with legitimate power upside, operating at a 21.5% K rate and 15.9% BB rate over a fresh AA sample—elite approach marks (85th and 89th percentiles in BB% and ISO respectively) anchored in the discipline to work counts. The MLB-equivalent translation projects his .226 ISO to .162 and his contact rate to remain above average, painting a second-division regular ceiling with meaningful hit-tool risk baked into the 60-grade hit grade. Sample is current and clean at 246 PA, though ValuCast's rankings have cooled slightly on Rincon over the past three days.

804942_pitcher.text: Cam Leiter is a high-velocity bat-misser with elite strikeout run—14.1 K/9 at the 97th percentile—who projects as a multi-inning or setup arm over the next two to three years. His 26.5% K-BB% (97th percentile) confirms the whiff profile, though command remains a weakness at 3.9 BB/9 (66th percentile), and his ERA of 3.09 in just 32 IP hints at inconsistent run prevention that will need to stabilize at higher levels. The sample is small and fresh from A-ball; confidence in the translation to MLB value is low, but the strikeout stuff is real enough to sustain the recent ranking climb.

804948_pitcher.text: Gage Stanifer is a high-strikeout arm still hunting for consistent command at Double-A, posting 11.1 K/9 (74th percentile) but struggling with walk rate at 5.2 BB/9 (38th percentile). His 4.26 ERA and 1.47 WHIP reflect the control battle—he's missing bats at a decent rate but leaving too many runners on base. The main risk is whether the command tightens enough to make him a usable starter; the ceiling is a useful MLB depth arm, though with only 57 innings in a current sample, there's limited certainty yet. ValuCast has him rising slightly in recent rankings.

804973_pitcher.text: Manuel Rodriguez is a control-first right-hander operating at AA who induces weak contact but lacks the strikeout stuff to carry a starter's workload. His 1.3 BB/9 (99th percentile) and 0.98 WHIP anchor an elite command profile, yet his 8.5 K/9 (29th percentile) sits well below league average, and a 4.55 ERA reflects the toll of that miss differential. The floor projects as a depth arm; the ceiling lands in useful multi-inning or setup relief, though the small margin between ceiling and floor suggests limited upside—he is cooling in ValuCast rankings after a recent dip in performance signals.

804981_pitcher.text: Riley Quick is a high-volume strikeout pitcher operating with legitimately poor command—a bat-missing profile constrained by walk rate. Over 33.3 IP at A+, he's punching out 13.2 K/9 (93rd percentile) while allowing 4.9 BB/9 (45th percentile), yielding a 4.86 ERA and 1.38 WHIP that undercut his stuff. The walk rate is the binding constraint; even elite strikeout stuff cannot carry a pitcher who cannot find the zone consistently, and his MLB-equivalent projection of 4.3 BB/9 against 9.1 K/9 suggests modest upside in an MLB role. Quick projects as a multi-inning or setup arm with medium risk on a two-to-three-year timeline, though the early sample is live and command development remains the entire story.

805082_hitter.text: Ronny Hernandez is a 21-year-old catcher showing disciplined contact and solid raw power in early-season action at A+. In 90 PA, he's posted a 18.2% strikeout rate (below the 22.0% MLB average) paired with 10.7% walks and a .176 ISO, all translating above the big-league norm. The main risk is the thin sample and his projection sitting heavily toward bench/platoon outcomes (74%), meaning even modest bat tools don't guarantee everyday visibility at catcher. ValuCast has him rising in recent rankings.

805127_hitter.text: Devin Taylor shows elite plate discipline paired with legitimate power — a 18.9% BB rate and .436 SLG at A+ anchored a .425 OBP across 254 PA there, with walk rate and OBP both in the 95th percentile. His current AA stint (53 PA) reveals concerning balance: .308 AVG and .558 SLG mask a collapse to 1.9% BB rate while maintaining a 22.6% K rate, stripping away the selectivity that made him work at the level below. The walk-rate cliff and tiny current sample create real doubt about whether the A+ profile travels, though his ISO percentile (47th) suggests the power may be more modest than the slugging line indicates.

805207_hitter.text: Caden Bodine is a contact-first hitter operating at an elite hit-tool level but constrained by modest power and a passive approach. His .35 AVG and 6.5% K% rank at the 99th percentile in the minor-league pool, while an .424 OBP sits at the 97th; however, his .15 ISO (52nd percentile) and 7.9% BB% (17th percentile) reveal limited impact upside and a reluctance to work counts. The projection ceiling is a bench or platoon bat, with an 85% probability of that role, underscoring that elite contact alone does not create everyday value at catcher. 805214_pitcher.text: Isaac Lyon is a 22-year-old right-handed depth arm still assembling his pitching foundation at AA, with control that ranks in the 87th percentile (2.9 BB/9) but strikeout stuff that lags significantly in the 30th percentile (8.6 K/9). The projection calls for useful MLB depth potential (67% probability), but the current 22-inning sample is thin, and he has more upside to tap than what today's early-season numbers reflect.

805255_pitcher.text: Dominick Reid is a low-miss, high-walk right-handed pitcher operating at Low-A with modest command and run prevention—he's striking out 9.1 per 9 but walking 3.6 per 9, yielding a 4.17 ERA over his current 49.7 innings. The K-BB% of 14.1% and BB/9 at the 73rd percentile mask a deeper issue: his 4.17 ERA and 1.29 WHIP rank just 66th and 73rd respectively, signaling that his strikeouts and walks aren't translating into competitive results. Reid projects as a depth arm with medium risk, most likely a useful MLB arm (68% probability) over the next two to three years, though his current run prevention grades remain a ceiling on upside. The sample is fresh and live, but still thin enough to warrant caution on the strength of any read.

805346_hitter.text: Ben Ross is a disciplined contact-first hitter whose walk rate (17.8%) ranks in the 93rd percentile but whose hit tool remains the constraint—he's batting .251 with a 24.3% strikeout rate over 214 PA at AAA. The power is adequate (ISO .188, 73rd percentile), but the batting average drag and modest exit results limit his ceiling to bench or platoon depth. On a 286 PA sample with no staleness risk, the approach skill is real, yet he needs to convert patience into more consistent contact to outgrow an organizational depth profile.

805347_hitter.text: Jim Jarvis is a contact-heavy hitter built on hit tool and plate discipline rather than raw power—he's punching out at 16.1% against a 13% walk rate while posting elite batting average in Triple-A. His .309 AVG and .402 OBP rank in the 91st and 96th percentiles, but the 19.2% strikeout rate when translated to MLB is a floor-setter, and his .134 ISO projects well below average impact. He profiles as a bench or platoon bat (85% probability) with a near-term path and modest upside, though this 322 PA sample is current and clean. ValuCast's rankings have moved him up +53 spots over three days.

805363_pitcher.text: Chris Clark is a miss-first right-handed pitcher operating as a near-term depth arm, built on the foundation of elite strikeout stuff (80-grade K/9) that translates to 8.0 K/9 in MLB terms. His AA track record—1.94 ERA, 0.97 WHIP, 17.5% K-BB%—supports that arsenal, even if AAA command has deteriorated sharply (5.4 BB/9 in the current 3.3 IP). The primary risk is control: a 25-grade BB/9 projection and 3.2 BB/9 in the MLB translation suggest he will leak baserunners despite the strikeouts, capping his ceiling at useful depth rather than starter potential. The current AAA sample is too thin to signal meaningful change in either direction.

805422_pitcher.text: Nate Snead is a right-handed depth pitcher showing modest control but limited carry — he sits at 5.9 K/9 (2nd percentile) and 3.0 BB/9 (85th percentile) over 21.3 IP at AA. The core problem is strikeout rate; his 7.4 K-BB% ranks in the 23rd percentile, and his translated K/9 of 7.4 against an MLB average of 8.6 leaves little margin for luck. His era and WHIP suggest he's managing outcomes reasonably well, but that run prevention cannot sustain without more miss in the zone. The sample is fresh and active, though still modest in depth.

805706_pitcher.text: AJ Russell is a high-strikeout arm who attacks hitters aggressively—his 14.51 K/9 at A-ball last season (26.7 IP) and 98th-percentile K/9 mark show elite whiff stuff. His K-BB% sits at 99th percentile (29.9%), indicating clean strike-zone command relative to his peers at that level. The main risk is extreme thinness: only 3 innings pitched at A+ this season, making any current reading unreliable; his prior A-ball season is the only substantial floor here, and the gap between lower minors and MLB is real. Confidence is low on role definition until he builds a meaningful sample above A.

805725_pitcher.text: Jake Miller shows control-first pitching early in his A+ stint, posting a 2.25 ERA with a 17.6 K-BB% over a thin 4 IP current sample. His MLB-equivalent translation suggests modest strikeout stuff (8.1 K/9) alongside a control profile that translates acceptably (13.2 K-BB%), though the walk rate climbs sharply in projection (2.9 BB/9 vs. 1.0 in the minor-league line). The sample is too small—only 9 IP of starter workload—to anchor confidence in either the control consistency or the depth of his role, and stale data within weeks could shift the picture quickly.

805779_hitter.text: Jacob Wilson is a light-contact shortstop who makes frequent contact but generates almost no leverage—his 9th percentile xwOBA and 84.2 mph average exit velo (2nd percentile) define a bat with little authority. He does avoid the strikezone well relative to his swing decisions, posting elite 11.7% strikeout rate and a rare high whiff-to-chase ratio, but that discipline yields only 4.7% walks and masks the core problem: he puts the ball in play softly and rarely hard. The projection line of .286/.328/.738 OPS is built on ball-in-play luck (70th percentile xBA against 9th percentile xwOBA signals hit-type dependency) and offers limited margin for error as a 24-year-old middle infielder with near-elite shortstop defense. Medium confidence reflects the disconnect between contact quality and batting average upside.

805790_pitcher.text: Cody Bowker is a strike-throwing right-hander building a case as a useful MLB depth arm, leaning on command and modest miss rather than dominance. His A-level track shows 14.52 K/9 and 4.54 BB/9 over 39.7 IP, placing him in the 98th percentile for strikeouts per nine and 97th for K-BB% among comparable pitchers. The hard ceiling is a mid-rotation starter—his current A+ sample of 8 IP is too thin to trust, and his MLB-equivalent translation (4.3 BB/9, 8.9 K/9 after age/level adjustment) suggests a reliever or depth starter who doesn't miss enough bats to dominate. The projection calls for two to three years; confidence is modest given only 8 innings at the new level.

805793_pitcher.text: Landen Maroudis is a young right-handed pitcher whose command has become the immediate problem—he's walking 5.1 per 9 innings (40th percentile) while generating only 7.0 K/9, leaving him with a 4.4% K-BB differential (12th percentile) over 42.7 innings at A+. His 7.17 ERA and 1.88 WHIP reflect a pitcher who is not missing enough bats and is giving up too many free passes to survive at the next level. The A+ sample is current and sufficient in volume to trust the read, though his modest strikeout rate limits upside even if command tightens.

805795_hitter.text: Aidan Miller is a disciplined, contact-first shortstop whose bat approach generates consistent on-base skills without much thump. He walked in 14.9% of his plate appearances at AA in 2025 while posting a .382 OBP, but the strikeout rate (23.7%) and modest .168 ISO expose his limited power ceiling and narrow margin for error. The main flaw is that he doesn't hit hard enough to profile as a regular—the MLB-equivalent translation projects just .135 ISO—leaving him as a bench or platoon bat at best. This is a stale prior-season sample now, and his ranking has moved up recently, but the modest power profile and strikeout volume remain the concrete constraint.

805796_hitter.text: Arjun Nimmala is a 20-year-old shortstop whose current-season profile at AA shows a contact-first bat with minimal thump—.308 AVG on just .061 ISO over 72 PA, posting an .744 OPS despite a 22.2% strikeout rate. His best work came at A+ (105 PA), where he hit .241 with .483 SLG and a 15.2% BB rate, signaling more power potential than what's shown recently, but the A+ line still projects to just .134 ISO in MLB translation. The main risk is that power has evaporated in his current AA stint, and at 20 with limited reps, it's unclear whether that's adjustment noise or a real loss of bat strength. He was placed on the injured list in late May, so confidence in this read is limited by both injury status and a thin 72-PA current sample.

805805_hitter.text: Walker Jenkins is a left-handed bat working advanced pitcher counts—drawing 17.4% walks against just 16.5% strikeouts, putting his approach in the 89th–92nd percentile. His .400 OBP and mild .151 ISO across 115 AAA plate appearances project to about .146 ISO and 10.9% BB% in MLB terms, a disciplined but thinner-than-average power profile. The real constraint is hit tool: his .258 minor-league average and modest OPS (.809) suggest he'll need to add bat-to-ball consistency to graduate beyond a bench or platoon role—a ceiling ValuCast assigns 85% probability. This is a thin, fresh AAA sample, and while Jenkins has climbed six spots in three days, the proof still lives in whether that plate discipline can sustain contact at the major-league level.

805808_hitter.text: Kevin McGonigle is a 21-year-old middle infielder with elite contact quality and discipline; his 86th-percentile xwOBA and 93rd-percentile walk rate project a .377 OBP foundation, while his 81st-percentile xBA suggests he'll consistently put the ball in play. The core risk is raw power—his exit velo sits 30th percentile and hard-hit rate 28th percentile, which caps his ceiling as a pure slugger and keeps his projected ISO modest despite solid bat-to-ball skills. His 99th-percentile chase rate and 94th-percentile whiff rate are immediate red flags on swing decisions, though the walk rate partially offsets that tendency. High confidence given the Statcast profile and full-season projection sample.

805809_pitcher.text: Travis Sykora is a high-miss, low-command starter profile—a right-hander who pounds the strike zone with velocity but lacks the precision to prevent hard contact at scale. Over 29.7 IP at A+, he posted a 1.21 ERA with a 14.3 K/9 and 36.8% K-BB%, elite rates that translate to a more modest 9.6 K/9 and 16.6% K-BB% at the MLB level, exposing significant gap between minor-league performance and major-league reality. The core risk is run prevention: despite the strikeouts, his ERA profile rests on a thin, stale sample under 30 innings from the prior season, and his command grade (65) trails his miss grade (80) by a wide margin, meaning home runs and walks will likely be a chronic issue. Given the staleness of the workload and his recent slide in ValuCast rankings, confidence is moderate at best until he logs fresh, extended innings.

805810_hitter.text: Blake Mitchell is a 21-year-old catcher operating as a high-variance offensive prospect built on elite plate discipline but crippled by contact issues. His 25.4% walk rate ranks in the 99th percentile, and he's posting a .850 OPS with .218 ISO over 272 PA at A+, but a 34.9% strikeout rate (8th percentile) is eating into that value and keeping his .213 average at the basement. The most immediate risk is that he'll never put the ball in play enough to become a usable bat; if the strikeouts don't improve, the walks alone won't sustain even a bench role. With only 272 plate appearances in a thin A+ sample and his approach still raw, confidence in a clear path is modest, though the power base and walk rate suggest more upside than today's hit tool shows.

805906_pitcher.text: Gage Wood is a high-strikeout, high-walk righthander whose electric miss (13.2 K/9, 92nd percentile) is sharp enough to play in relief, but whose command (3.6 BB/9, 70th percentile) is loose enough that he will likely never start. His 3.6 ERA and 1.2 WHIP have generated early impact in AA/A ball, but he has barely pitched in anger—just 47 innings—and the projection flags limited pitching shape and multi-inning risk as the main ceiling constraint. ValuCast is moving him up sharply in its rankings, though the modest sample and command profile limit conviction that the strikeout rate will hold.

805953_hitter.text: Anthony Huezo is a 20-year-old left-handed hitter generating genuine power—.298 ISO in the 98th percentile—but strangled by swing-and-miss; his 31.3% strikeout rate ranks in the 18th percentile and will cap his floor hard if it doesn't improve. His .909 OPS on 268 plate appearances is real and translates to solid impact, yet the contact collapse is the legitimate risk: when the strikeouts run that high, the hit tool (.259 AVG, 67th percentile) can't recover the value. ValuCast projects him as organizational depth with upside, arriving in two to three years, but the strikeout problem is the gate he must pass through first.

806010_pitcher.text: Barrett Kent is a young starter with elite early command results but a control leak that requires monitoring—27.3 innings of 1.98 ERA and 7.2 K/9 mask a 5.3 BB/9 rate (36th percentile) that sits well above MLB average when translated. The strikeout rate itself ranks at just the 10th percentile for his peer pool, suggesting modest raw stuff paired with decent present command, but the walk rate is the real concern at 4.5 BB/9 translated. This is a stale, thin starter sample from prior-season A-ball; confidence in any read here is low given the 27-inning workload and lack of recent activity.

806046_pitcher.text: Alex Clemmey is a 20-year-old left-handed starter showing the strikeout rate of a mid-rotation arm—10.0 K/9 in 61.3 AA innings—but control is a significant brake on his upside. His 6.3 BB/9 sits in the 22nd percentile; the MLB translation suggests that projects to 5.3 BB/9 at the big-league level, still well above league average. The gap between whiff rate (57th percentile in K/9) and command (22nd percentile in BB/9) creates a volatile profile, and his 5.14 ERA reflects that inconsistency. ValuCast projects him as a multi-inning relief arm or setup option with a depth-arm floor over one to two years, though the recent ranking movement suggests cooling in the evaluator's view.

806061_hitter.text: Isaiah Drake is a left-handed hitter showing a pull-heavy, power-first approach that hasn't yet translated into consistent contact or on-base skill at A+ ball. Over 296 PA he's hitting .251 with a .411 SLG but a 26.4% strikeout rate and modest 10.1% walk rate—the swings-and-misses are the primary brake on his overall offensive value. His hit and approach grades both sit at 45-level, reflecting a 53 OPS and modest percentile standing, and even his power (ISO .16, 58th percentile) has not offset the offensive drain. The projection floor is organizational depth with a two-to-three-year timeline; current performance suggests medium risk to that floor given the early-stage strikeout profile.

806064_pitcher.text: Steven Echavarria is a 20-year-old righty working through A+ ball with mediocre present strikeout and command numbers—8.0 K/9 and 4.6 BB/9 both well below average in his peer pool—that translate to 7.1 K/9 and 4.5 BB/9 in MLB terms. His 6.23 ERA and 1.45 WHIP reflect immediate results that are more concerning than his modest stuff grades suggest, with ERA landing in the 23rd percentile. The real risk is that his strikeout-to-walk differential is too thin (8.4 K-BB%) to support starter viability or consistent MLB depth value without sharp improvement in either miss or command. ValuCast has him cooling in recent rankings, and with only 60.7 innings on the board, the sample alone carries low confidence in any specific outcome trajectory.

806071_hitter.text: Jonny Farmelo is a young left-handed hitter with a disciplined approach and above-average power stroke, built on a 16.2% walk rate and .203 ISO across 315 A+ plate appearances. His 87th-percentile BB% and 80th-percentile ISO anchor an .852 OPS, though a 26.0% strikeout rate—44th percentile—prevents him from being a plus hitter; in MLB equivalent translation, that K% rises to 28.4%. The ceiling is a bench or platoon bat (83% probability), with modest upside if the contact rate improves, and the sample is fresh and sizable enough to trust the shape.

806077_hitter.text: Kendall George is a high-contact left-handed hitter with elite bat control who is generating walk rates above league average, but he is severely limited by power—his .064 ISO ranks at just the 6th percentile among hitters. The current sample is active and clean, though power limitations are a structural risk, not a volatility concern.

806146_hitter.text: George Lombard Jr. is a disciplined contact hitter built on patient at-bats and balanced offensive shape rather than raw power or batting average. The catch is a .256 AVG with modest 8 home runs and .187 ISO, indicating he lacks the hit tool or thump needed to profile as more than a bench regular—and at shortstop, that profile faces real positional pressure. Lombard's ceiling projects to second division regular with 72% odds he lands as bench or platoon depth; ValuCast's ranking has cooled 3 spots in three days, reflecting the gap between his approach grade (70) and his ability to translate that discipline into production.

806191_hitter.text: Tai Peete is a high-leverage power bat in early A+ ball who trades contact for explosive slugging — his .256 ISO ranks 95th percentile among hitters with 100+ PA, but a 31.4% strikeout rate undercuts the hit tool and approach. At 20 years old with just 140 plate appearances, the sample is fresh and current, though small enough that his true skill remains unsettled; ValuCast projects him as organizational depth over two to three years, with an 85% likelihood of a bench or platoon role. The main risk is whether he can sustain this power profile while cutting the whiffs—translated to MLB, his strikeout rate edges above league average and his isolated power would shrink considerably.

806210_hitter.text: Alfonsin Rosario is a high-leverage power hitter whose plate discipline remains the primary concern: he's posted a 33.6% strikeout rate over 211 PA at AA, well above the 22% MLB average, despite carrying a .536 slugging mark and 97th-percentile ISO. His translated profile shows a 30.5% K% and .185 ISO when adjusted to MLB baseline, which sustains legitimate 75-grade power but exposes a hit-tool floor that could cap him at bench production. ValuCast projects a bench or platoon ceiling (85% probability) within one to two years, with the caveat that his current shape shows more upside than today's value suggests. The sample is fresh and sufficient, but his strikeout rate will be the binding constraint on offensive consistency.

806221_hitter.text: Easton Shelton is a 20-year-old power-first hitter with exceptional bat speed and leverage; his .620 slugging and .341 ISO rank in the 99th percentile despite operating in A-ball. The underlying read is loud: he strikes out at 36.6%, well above the 22% MLB average even after translation to 37.7%, which is the main developmental obstacle and a meaningful drag on offensive floor. His walk rate (12.7%) and contact quality are genuine strengths, but the swing-and-miss is severe enough at this stage that consistency and on-base reliability remain unproven questions. The 268 PA sample is current and clean, but translating elite raw power in A-ball to sustained major-league production requires demonstrable strikeout management.

806224_pitcher.text: Brady Smith is a high-strikeout arm still in the early stages, missing bats at an elite rate (15.0 K/9, 98th percentile K-BB% at 27%) but struggling with command in the A-ball sample. His 4.29 ERA and 1.36 WHIP reflect walk issues (4.3 BB/9, 57th percentile) that will need to tighten for consistent advancement. The 42-inning current sample is fresh but thin, and the low-confidence MLB translation suggests skepticism about how his strikeout dominance will age at higher levels.

806233_hitter.text: Luke Stevenson is a left-handed catcher with an exceptional approach—drawing walks at a 99th-percentile rate (22.7%)—but his contact and power remain well behind the hit-tool demands of a regular. Over 247 PA at A+, he pairs that elite walk rate with a 27.1% strikeout rate and a .217 AVG/.391 SLG, suggesting a player who can work counts but struggles to convert pitches into barrels. The main risk is that his 50-grade hit and impact tools leave little margin for error; even with plus plate discipline, a catcher without average or power will be roofed as depth. 808265_hitter.text: Franklin Arias is a 20-year-old shortstop who is hitting at impact register in AA: elite bat control paired with rare power production. His ceiling is an impact regular, though the recent ValuCast ranking movement has cooled slightly as the sample has grown.

808277_hitter.text: Miguel Rodríguez is a 20-year-old catcher showing rare plate discipline—a 22.4% BB% paired with only 10.4% K%—that translates to MLB-equivalent walk rate of 10.8%, well above the league average of 8.5%. 808510_pitcher.text: Manuel Genao is a 20-year-old right-hander showing uncommon walk discipline for his age and level, paired with middling strikeout stuff. 808535_hitter.text: John Gil is a balanced, contact-oriented hitter showing better command of the zone than raw power at age 20 in A+ ball. 808675_hitter.text: Ramon Ramirez is a catcher with loud raw power—.487 SLG and .202 ISO are 85th-percentile marks—but a strikeout problem that limits how often he makes contact. 808825_pitcher.text: Andrew Sears operates as a high-velocity contact pitcher in limited AA exposure, posting a 1.17 ERA with 12.9 K/9 and a 0.65 WHIP over his first 7.7 innings. 808967_pitcher.text: Yamamoto is a high-command starter who controls the zone at an elite level and generates above-average whiff rates without relying on overwhelming stuff. 808982_hitter.text: Jung Hoo Lee is a high-contact hitter operating at an elite hit-tool level but generating below-average exit velo and hard-hit rates that cap his power ceiling. High confidence in this profile given the Statcast sample and his established hit-first approach.

809092_hitter.text: Murf Gray is a power-first right-handed hitter with real loft—ISO of .344 and 99th percentile slugging at age 22—who is hitting .323 with a 1.077 OPS over 117 PA at A+. 809093_pitcher.text: Aidan Cremarosa is a control-first right-handed pitcher operating at A-ball with elite command and walk suppression; his 1.7 BB/9 (98th percentile) and 27.1% K-BB% (98th percentile) anchor a 2.56 ERA across 52.7 innings. 809100_pitcher.text: Ixan Henderson is a left-handed pitcher selling out on ERA and contact management while living with a below-average strikeout rate—he posted a 2.60 ERA and 1.10 WHIP in 132 innings at AA, but his 9.1 K/9 sits only in the 38th percentile and his K-BB% of 16% lags the mid-tier threshold. This is a stale prior-season sample (132 IP from 2025) with moderate confidence in the MLB-equivalent translation, and Henderson has climbed 176 spots in ValuCast's rankings over three days.

809229_pitcher.text: Jaron DeBerry is a right-handed pitcher building a starter profile on volume, but control remains a meaningful drag on his upside. His MLB-equivalent translation projects 4.3 BB/9 against a league average of 3.2, placing him well above the median walk rate; strikeout production (8.0 K/9 equivalent) sits below league average. The core risk is not strikeout scarcity—it's the inability to locate consistently enough to survive repeated exposure to big-league lineups. This is a modest 65-inning sample at AA, so early-season form shapes the read more than a full body of work.

809254_pitcher.text: Anthony Eyanson is a 21-year-old right-handed pitcher operating with exceptional early command and low free passes at AA, posting a 1.46 ERA with a 15.6% K-BB% and 4.7 BB/9 over a modest 24.7 innings. The real risk is the minimal sample size and unknown pitch arsenal; 45 innings is too thin to confirm whether this control profile holds, and without shape or velocity data, there's no way to assess the ceiling or likelihood of regression. Given the active, current sample and moderate translation confidence, this is a pure upside play that demands a full season of evidence before trusting the results.

809343_pitcher.text: Bryce Mayer is a high-velocity bat-missing arm whose strikeout shape is his carrying tool—13.8 K/9 at AA ranks 96th percentile—but the walk rate (5.9 BB/9, 26th percentile) is dragging down the overall control profile and limiting upside. This read is built on just 38.3 innings at the upper minors, so confidence is low until he logs more consecutive innings at this level.

809372_hitter.text: Victor Figueroa is a 22-year-old left-handed first baseman who can hit for loud power but operates with a strikeout-heavy swing—he's posting .606 slugging and .337 ISO (99th percentile) against a 31.6% strikeout rate (17th percentile) in 247 plate appearances at A+. His walk rate sits at 10.5%, solid for the level, but his .269 average and .348 OBP show the contact struggles that come with his approach; the MLB-equivalent translation suggests he'd carry a 31.7% K rate and .194 ISO at the major-league level, well below the thresholds for impact production. ValuCast is moving Condon up in rankings on the strength of this performance.

813989_pitcher.text: Talon Haley is a left-handed pitcher who misses bats at an elite rate but struggles to find the zone, a profile that currently feels more depth-arm than starter. 814005_pitcher.text: Jake Bloss is a control-dependent depth arm working through a thin early-season sample at AAA. The critical risk is that 19 innings of minor-league data, compressed into just 4 IP of current work, cannot reliably predict his performance; confidence in any read here is low given the sample size, and more rope is needed before projecting his role.

814172_hitter.text: Chase Jaworsky is a 21-year-old shortstop mired in a prolonged offensive slump with no immediate path to impact. The core problem is a near-complete lack of power (ISO in the 5th percentile) paired with a strikeout rate above league average even when translated to MLB; no walk rate bump can offset that damage. The sample is current and clean, but the depth of the hit and power collapse leaves little room for optimism in the near term.

814307_hitter.text: Zyhir Hope generates power—.472 SLG and .2 ISO rank 82nd and 79th respectively among prospect hitters—but the strikeout rate is the real story. The 299-PA sample is current and clean, but the skill shape—hit and approach both graded 40–50—remains the constraint on his upside.

814351_pitcher.text: Lucas Braun shows modest command but lacks the strikeout stuff to operate efficiently at the Triple-A level—his MLB-equivalent 7.1 K/9 and 3.0 BB/9 translate to a K-BB% around 10.5%, well below the 13.5% major-league average and ranking in just the 21st percentile among ValuCast pitchers. The main risk is a lack of dominant pitch production; without significant velocity or movement profile gains, he will struggle to miss bats or work ahead in counts. This is a fresh sample with good volume context, but the skill ceiling is that of a back-end depth arm.

814354_pitcher.text: Yanzel Correa is a strikeout-heavy right-handed pitcher early in his A-level exposure who can miss bats—11.5 K/9 sits at the 79th percentile—but is struggling with command that will need to tighten before he advances. The arm profile shows present stuff, but 29.7 innings is a thin foundation for confidence in the trajectory; the walk rate is the immediate work item that will determine whether the strikeout gift translates to success.

814392_pitcher.text: Xavier Rivas is a high-velocity strikeout arm operating deep in the zone with heavy walk rates—a bat-missing profile held back by command inconsistency. He's punching out 13.5 K/9 (94th percentile) while sitting at 22.1% K-BB%, but his 5.0 BB/9 and 5.36 ERA show he's not locating that stuff consistently enough yet. The walk rate is the dominant flaw; even when translated to MLB equivalents, he'd sit at 4.3 BB/9, well above league average. With 45 innings at AA, the strikeout stuff is real, but the control has to tighten before he becomes a reliable depth option.

814409_hitter.text: Seaver King is a high-contact hitter with modest plate discipline who leans on hit tool and power to generate offense. His .296 AVG and .487 SLG rank at the 91st and 85th percentiles respectively, but a 4.0% BB% and 20.8% K% expose a passivity problem—he ranks in the 1st percentile for walk rate and doesn't defend himself enough at the plate. The core risk is organizational depth ceiling; even with upside trajectory, he projects 83% to bench/platoon role given the approach limitations. This is a small sample (125 PA) on a shortstop still finding his way.

814414_hitter.text: Kyle DeBarge is a 22-year-old shortstop hitting into a K-heavy approach: 28.0% strikeout rate and just .197 AVG across 271 PA at AA, putting him in the bottom quartile for contact. His 12.2% walk rate keeps his approach from capsizing entirely, and there's some iso juice at .149, but a .649 OPS in the lower percentiles signals a profile that hasn't yet produced. The main problem is hit tool—contact is genuinely poor right now, and even with above-average walk rate, the batting average leakage and strikeout volume make it hard to project everyday impact. Sample is current and clear, but this is a player whose bat shape leans toward depth or bench outcome unless the swing-and-miss tightens significantly.

814430_hitter.text: Brett Callahan is a left-handed hitter showing legitimate thump from a light-contact profile. In 259 PA at AA, he's posted .511 SLG and .242 ISO (90th and 91st percentile), backed by a .375 OBP that reflects a strong 13.1% walk rate. The strikeout floor is real—23.1% K% in MLB translation—and paired with modest contact quality (.269 AVG), his offensive ceiling depends entirely on sustaining his power; if the strikeouts climb or the ISO regresses, he profiles as a depth piece rather than a regular. The sample is current and sizeable enough to trust the power read, though his path to playing time at CF will require showing he can hit enough to offset the swing-and-miss.

814439_hitter.text: Ryan Waldschmidt is a contact-first bat who punches above his power grade through excellent command of the strike zone and an elite hit tool. His AAA line shows .302 AVG, .418 OBP, and .528 SLG across 195 PA, with a 13% walk rate and 24% strikeout rate—all metrics in the 87th–94th percentile tier. The risk is that 24% K rate translates to 23.7% at the MLB level, above-average but not thin enough to cover a power floor stuck at .165 ISO in equivalent terms; he projects as a second-division regular with a 68% likelihood of bench-or-platoon usage. ValuCast has moved him up 24 spots in three days, suggesting growing conviction in the contact foundation, though the current 195 PA sample is fresh and directly observed.

814444_hitter.text: Will Turner is a left-handed hitter built on elite plate discipline—22.2% BB% (99th percentile)—paired with above-average power (.203 ISO, 80th percentile), but he's a hit-tool problem who can't make consistent contact at .202 AVG despite a .395 OBP. The strikeout rate (21.8% K%) and weak batting average translate to just a .152 MLB-equivalent ISO and expose him as a high-leverage, low-floor depth bat rather than an impact prospect. This is a bench/platoon outcome (85% probability) capped at organizational depth, with only five percent odds of a regular role; the sample is clean at 225 PA but recent ranking movement suggests cooling sentiment in the system.

814450_hitter.text: Wehiwa Aloy is a 22-year-old shortstop generating real power—his .205 ISO ranks 79th percentile in the ValuCast pool—but leaning heavily on strikeouts (26.9 K%) to get there, with a modest walk rate (9.5%) that leaves little margin for error in the contact game. His .277 average and .344 OBP reflect a player betting on raw strength over pitch recognition or bat control. The chief risk is that strikeout rate; translated to MLB context, it sits 28.5%, above league average, and the walk rate doesn't compensate enough to offset the whiffs. The 253 PA sample is fresh and sufficient, so the mixed profile is real.

814455_hitter.text: Nick Mitchell is a disciplined contact hitter whose walk rate (18.5%) ranks in the 94th percentile but whose bat lacks impact—he's managed only .095 ISO with a .296 SLG over 211 PA at AA. His strikeout rate (19.0%) and overall .650 OPS signal he's not converting that patience into hard contact or run production. The floor is organizational depth, and with power and overall hit grades both well below average (30 and 45 respectively), the upside depends almost entirely on whether the approach translates to better results as he progresses.

814489_pitcher.text: Brett Wichrowski is a 23-year-old right-handed pitcher working at AAA with stalled command and strikeout rates that don't compensate for it. His AAA-equivalent translation shows 8.1 K/9 with a 3.8 BB/9, leaving him near league average in K-BB% at 11.5%—well below the 13.5% median for his pitcher pool. The major red flag is his current AAA sample: 8.36 ERA over just 14 innings with a 7.8% K-BB%, and while that's a thin slice, his AA work (6.42 ERA, 1.51 WHIP) confirms the walk rate and lack of dominant stuff. Confidence is limited; 14 innings is too small to build on, but the AA tape backs the concerning signal.

814490_pitcher.text: Ethan Pecko is a depth-minded right-hander whose command is functional but whose strikeout punch is light for a prospect. In 44.7 IP at AAA, he posted a 3.63 ERA with 7.9 K/9 and 3.4 BB/9—a K-BB% of 12.0 that ranks only 46th percentile in the ValuCast pitcher pool, despite respectable ERA and WHIP rates (76th and 79th percentiles, respectively). The core issue is insufficient miss; at his current pace, MLB translation suggests 8.1 K/9, well below league average, which limits ceiling to useful depth arm rather than rotation contributor. Pecko is rising in ValuCast rankings, suggesting some underlying skill may be emerging in the current sample, but confidence remains moderate given the thin strikeout floor.

814527_pitcher.text: Patrick Copen is a right-handed pitcher sitting in the low percentiles for command, allowing 6.9 BB/9 (17th percentile) and posting a 7.44 ERA across 61.7 innings at AA. He does miss bats at a league-average clip—10.2 K/9 (60th percentile)—but the walk rate overwhelms the strikeout production, yielding a K-BB% of just 7.9% (25th percentile). The core problem is control; until he cuts the free passes in half, high ERA and WHIP will drag down any value, even if the raw stuff plays. ValuCast projects him as depth-arm material with a 61% chance of becoming a useful MLB arm one to two years out, but today's walk rate suggests the floor is equally likely.

815043_pitcher.text: Simon Miller shows early strikeout authority—10.2 K/9 in his current AA sample—but the walk rate (1.9 BB/9) translates to 3.0 BB/9 at the MLB level, a meaningful control risk. His K-BB% of 22.5% shrinks to 13.9% when adjusted for big-league conditions, eroding the margin for error. With only 9.7 innings pitched, confidence in any read here is low; this is a depth arm sketch, not a rounded evaluation.

815071_pitcher.text: Marcus Phillips is a young right-handed pitcher working to establish command and consistency at A+, showing strikeout ability (10.6 K/9, 66th percentile) but hamstrung by a walk rate (7.6 BB/9, 11th percentile) that kills his ability to dominate. Over 35.7 innings, his 6.81 ERA and 1.82 WHIP reflect a pitcher who misses bats but can't keep runners off base—a profile that translates to an MLB-equivalent 5.7 BB/9, well above league average. The floor is depth relief; the ceiling is a useful mid-rotation arm if he can tighten command. This is a thin sample early in 2026, and ValuCast has him rising in the rankings, but the walk rate is the real obstacle before he matters at the major-league level.

815111_pitcher.text: Keegan Zinn shows a rare strikeout-to-walk shape for a 21-year-old at A-ball: 12.9 K/9 ranks at the 90th percentile, while his K-BB% of 13.9% sits around the 56th percentile, a genuine skill signal in a small sample. The problem is control—7.0 BB/9 is the 14th percentile and translates to an MLB-equivalent 5.5 BB/9, well above league average—and his 5.63 ERA reflects both the walks and a WHIP near 1.70. The 32-inning sample is current and clean, but too thin to lock in the strikeout rate or know if the command issues are fixable.

815119_pitcher.text: Tanner Franklin is a strikeout-heavy young right-hander leaning on his fastball with elevated walk rates that cut against his arsenal's upside. Through 45.3 innings at A+, he's spinning 11.3 K/9 (77th percentile) while issuing 4.6 BB/9 (50th percentile), leaving his K-BB% at 17.0% (76th percentile)—strong whiff numbers undermined by command slippage that bleeds runs (5.36 ERA, 1.39 WHIP). The floor is a depth arm; the ceiling is useful major-league contributor, though ValuCast projects the command will need to tighten and more upside exists than current results suggest. This is a small, early sample with low MLB-translation confidence.

815147_hitter.text: Wilson Rodriguez is a young left-handed bat who works counts aggressively—his 15.8% BB% ranks in the 84th percentile—but lacks the hit tool to consistently convert that patience into production. Through 278 PA at A+, he's hitting .250 with a .397 SLG and .769 OPS, while striking out at a 19.1% rate that still translates to a concerning 23.1% K% at the MLB level. The core problem is a 50th-percentile ISO and 45-grade power projection; his approach strength masks a shallow offensive profile with minimal impact ceiling. ValuCast projects him as organizational depth with an 85% probability of a bench-or-platoon role, arriving two to three years out, so there is room for improvement at present depth levels, but the early read is more disciplined minor-leaguer than future producer.

815148_pitcher.text: Nestor German is a high-walk right-handed pitcher operating as a starter at AAA, built around above-average strikeout stuff but hampered by a control leak that translates upward. His 10.2 K/9 projects to 8.8 K/9 in MLB and ranks 60th percentile, but a 3.6 BB/9 (73rd percentile) sits above league average and makes his K-BB% of 17.1% look better than the on-field results—his 4.54 ERA and 1.36 WHIP reveal a pitcher who is giving back value in the zone. The core risk is that command hasn't followed stuff; at 24 with 69 IP this season, he has enough rope to find it, but the walks have to come down for him to sustain starter role value.

815154_hitter.text: Slade Caldwell is a 20-year-old left-handed hitter working through A+ ball who draws walks at an elite rate (16.7% BB%) but cannot generate enough hard contact to offset a punishing strikeout profile (29.8% K%), yielding a .307 SLG and .683 OPS over 258 plate appearances. The walk rate ranks in the 88th percentile, yet his ISO sits in the 15th percentile and his AVG at 28th—the contact and power ceiling remain stubbornly low despite the selectivity. The core risk is straightforward: a high-walk, high-strikeout profile that translates to organizational depth rather than impact in a full-season environment. Sample is current and sizable enough to trust the read.

815179_pitcher.text: Christian Herberholz operates as a depth-type starter with middling strikeout stuff—his 8.1 K/9 in the MLB-equivalent translation sits below league average—paired with a walk rate (3.5 BB/9) that matches the major-league mean but limits upside. In minor-league context over 27 innings he's posted a 4.33 ERA with a 1.56 WHIP, placing him in the bottom half of his peer group for both metrics. The primary risk is modest stuff-to-results translation; his K-BB% of 11.9 suggests thin margin for error as a back-of-rotation option. This read carries only medium confidence given 44 innings total at AAA and no track record of sustained upper-level success.

815212_pitcher.text: Keyner Martinez is a pure bat-missing arm whose stuff plays well above his results—he's striking out 14.7 per 9 (98th percentile) in a current 49-inning A-ball sample, but command is a serious drag. He's walking 5.9 per 9 (27th percentile) with a WHIP of 1.45, which explains why his 4.96 ERA sits at only the 48th percentile despite elite strikeout stuff. The projection ceiling is a useful MLB depth arm, but he needs substantial command development to become anything more than a back-of-the-rotation option. The sample is fresh and active, though 49 innings is still a limited runway on which to build confidence in either direction.

815219_pitcher.text: Luis De La Torre is a 22-year-old left-handed pitcher showing elite strikeout stuff—12.0 K/9 at A+ puts him in the 83rd percentile—but struggling to harness it in games. His 6.7 BB/9 (19th percentile) and resulting 4.76 ERA reveal the core problem: he's missing bats at an above-average rate yet walking too many to get outs efficiently, landing him at 10.8 K-BB% (53rd percentile) when translated to MLB-equivalent rate. The main risk is command consistency; even in a shallow 51-inning sample, the walk rate is too high to project him as a reliable starter. ValuCast sees him trending upward, with a depth-arm ceiling and a 68% probability he becomes a useful MLB arm once he tightens his control.

815298_pitcher.text: Jacob Bresnahan is a left-handed pitcher working in A+ ball with a strikeout profile (10.4 K/9) that grades above-average but constrained by below-average command, as reflected in his 4.8 BB/9 (47th percentile) and 3.92 ERA over 41.3 innings. His K-BB% of 14.7% sits at the 63rd percentile—respectable but not elite—and an ERA of 3.92 lands him in the 70th percentile, a gap that signals control issues are eating into his run prevention despite decent miss rates. The core flaw is command: a 35-grade on BB/9 significantly undercuts his strikeout ability, and that imbalance will determine whether he reaches a useful MLB role (61% odds) or settles into depth/relief work (34%). The sample is current and sufficient, but he remains two to three years from the majors with medium risk.

815304_hitter.text: Josh Adamczewski is a high-contact left-handed hitter with elite bat control and patience at the plate, posting .464 OBP and 19.4% BB% across his best 211-PA sample at A+. His current AA exposure (24 PA) is too sparse to read, but the A+ line shows 98th-percentile AVG and 99th-percentile OBP, underpinned by a 16.7% K% that translates to well above-average contact discipline. The real problem is power: his ISO sits at .091 in the tiny AA sample and .241 at A+, leaving him dependent on a hit tool to have any value, with the 45th-percentile approach grade suggesting he lacks the aggression or leverage to drive the ball consistently. Confidence is limited by the current 24-PA AA run; the A+ foundation is solid enough to sustain the projection, but power development will determine whether he becomes anything beyond organizational depth.

815348_pitcher.text: Boston Bateman is a left-handed pitcher working starter volume who shows strong strikeout stuff—11.1 K/9, 76th percentile—but is bleeding walks at 4.6 BB/9, 50th percentile, with a resulting 4.05 ERA. The core issue is command; his K-BB% of 16.9% (76th) masks a control problem that will limit his ceiling even as he develops. Bateman projects as a multi-inning or setup arm over the next two to three years, though the recent rank cooling reflects the reality that walk rate at age 20 on a 53-inning sample is still a legitimate signal of command risk.

815352_hitter.text: Caleb Bonemer is a high-leverage power bat in a young, strikeout-prone package. His A+ sample shows .556 slugging and 99th-percentile ISO (.318), plus a 13.7% walk rate that grades well, but the 29.1% strikeout rate is a major structural problem that has survived the move to AA. MLB-equivalent translation pegs him at a 30.5% K%, well above league average, which will limit his ability to sustain the power or get consistent at-bats even as a platoon option. The current AA sample is just 25 PA and offers no new signal, so the A+ read remains the best evidence available.

The core flaw is power scarcity: his ISO translates to just .157 in MLB equivalents, barely above league average, and his skill grades project only 20th-percentile power and impact upside despite the .577 SLG. The .288 OBP and contact issues create a ceiling of organizational depth rather than a core regular, though his ISO suggests some upside if he can tighten his plate discipline over the next two to three years. Sample is active and current as of late June with no staleness concern.

815501_pitcher.text: Bryce Meccage is a 20-year-old right-handed starter who is giving up walks at an unsustainable rate while his strikeout rate lags behind league average. 815549_pitcher.text: Ryan Sloan is a 20-year-old right-handed starter living on command and strike-zone discipline — he sits in the 94th percentile for BB/9 (2.1) and 93rd for K-BB% (24%), controlling his walks while punching out 11.0 K/9 in the 70th percentile across 51.7 AA innings. His run prevention doesn't match his stuff yet: the 4.3 ERA and 1.3 WHIP grade only at the 50th–59th percentiles, a real flaw that may signal either sequencing issues or plain bad luck that will resolve with age and experience. 815552_pitcher.text: Levi Sterling is a 19-year-old right-handed A-ball starter working starter volume (62.7 IP) with modest stuff and command issues that limit his upside—9.5 K/9 ranks only 48th percentile, while his 3.6 BB/9 sits at 73rd percentile, showing better control relative to his strikeout rate. 815598_pitcher.text: Dasan Hill is a pure strikeout arm with a devastating whiff rate but significant command inconsistency. The floor is a useful depth arm; upside points toward a back-of-the-rotation starter or late-inning reliever if he tightens his control, though the small 35-inning sample limits confidence in the current trajectory.

815608_hitter.text: Wyatt Sanford is a left-handed hitter with rare power generation living inside a strikeout-heavy profile—he's posted .252 ISO (94th percentile) and .964 OPS (98th) over 224 PA at A+, but whiffs at 31.2% (18th percentile), well above the MLB average of 22%. ValuCast projects him as a second-division regular with a floor of reserve—83% probability he lands as bench/platoon—because the power is legitimate but the hit tool is contingent on age-related refinement over the next two to three years. The sample is live and current with no injury risk noted.

815617_hitter.text: Kayson Cunningham is a 20-year-old left-handed hitter showing elite contact skills but struggling with selectivity and power consistency at the A+ level. 815626_pitcher.text: Ethan Bagwell is a command-first A-level starter who pounds the zone—1.04 WHIP, 87th percentile in BB/9—but lacks the strikeout stuff to dominate; his 9.1 K/9 rates only 40th percentile and translates to 7.1 K/9 in MLB terms. At 20 with 68 innings, the sample is current and live, and ValuCast's projection is a useful MLB arm over two to three years—upside exists—but this is a depth starter profile with meaningful downside risk if fastball velocity or secondary pitch shape don't develop further.

815785_pitcher.text: Braylon Doughty is a command-first righthander operating well ahead of the control curve at age 20, striking out 11.2 per 9 while walking just 1.8—both elite marks relative to his A+ peer group (97th and 76th percentiles respectively). The ceiling is back-end starter, but his 3.35 ERA and 1.27 WHIP hint at a gap between his stuff and results; the MLB-equivalent translation shows walk rate climbing to 2.7 per 9 and strikeout rate dipping to 8.5, a common reality check for young minor-league pitchers. Doughty is rising in ValuCast rankings and profiles as more upside than present value, but he needs to prove he can sustain command while generating strikeouts at the next level.

The strikeout rate is the tangible constraint: 28.3% contact rate suggests he'll need to tighten the zone recognition as he climbs, and the MLB-equivalent translation pegs that at 29%, well above league average. The current sample is fresh and large enough to trust the power and patience; the question is whether those tools can coexist with major-league strike-zone discipline.

815789_pitcher.text: David Shields is a left-handed pitcher who misses bats reliably—10.4 K/9 across 58 innings at A+—but is giving up too much hard contact to stick as a starter, evidenced by his 4.03 ERA despite a 1.12 WHIP that ranks 91st percentile. The main risk is run prevention; his ERA and contact management don't match his stuff profiles, and the modest sample leaves real uncertainty about whether that gap closes with experience. He ranks 107 overall and has cooled slightly in ValuCast rankings over the past three days.

815792_hitter.text: Chase Harlan is a high-contact, power-producing hitter who generates elite bat speed and collision—his best A-level line shows .329 AVG with .242 ISO and 99th percentile OPS—but he struggles to work counts, posting a 20% strikeout rate in translation. The strikeout problem is real and structural; his approach grade projects at 25, meaning he chases aggressively and rarely walks (0% BB in his current 5-PA cup of coffee). ValuCast projects him as a bench or platoon bat with 85% probability, arriving in two to three years. The current A+ sample is just five plate appearances and too thin to read his immediate trajectory, though his prior A performance suggests the profile is holding.

815795_pitcher.text: Junior Ciprian is a controlled, efficient low-velocity arm currently operating as a depth starter; his 2.83 ERA and .94 WHIP (97th percentile) anchor a profile defined by exceptional contact management rather than swing-and-miss. He strikes out 9.9 per 9 (56th percentile) but walks just 3.8 per 9 (69th percentile), yielding a 17.6% K-BB% (78th percentile) that translates cleanly to modest MLB rates. The sample is current and meaningful, but at 18 with moderate command and modest thump so far, this looks like a years-away organizational depth profile rather than a near-term contributor.

829210_hitter.text: Ty Harvey is a 19-year-old catcher showing early discipline at the plate—19% BB% on a 58 PA sample—but swinging and missing at a concerning clip (24.1% K%). His .107 ISO translates to below-average raw power for a catcher, and the strikeout rate (24.1%), even accounting for youth, sits above league average in the MLB equivalent read. The sample is small and fresh, so expect volatility as he faces stiffer velocity and sequencing.

829854_hitter.text: Luis Arana is an 18-year-old A-level shortstop who commands the strike zone exceptionally—posting 19.2% BB% over 78 PA—but whose overall bat lacks impact, evidenced by a modest .127 ISO and a .460 SLG despite the strong .462 OBP. The approach grade is elite relative to his peer group; the hit tool is solid; but power and overall impact are well below average, and that power ceiling is the central constraint. At 78 plate appearances in a current season sample, confidence in the profile is limited, though the plate discipline suggests a repeatable skill.

830239_hitter.text: Aaron Walton is a power-dominant hitter with the bat speed to impact games but a swing-and-miss problem that could limit his floor. His .513 SLG and .24 ISO rank in the 91st percentile at his level, but he's striking out in 28.4% of his at-bats—well above league average even in translation. The 285 PA sample is clean and current, though MLB-equivalent projection shows his strikeout rate holding near 30%, which will compress his offensive value if it persists at the majors.

830336_pitcher.text: Mason Peters is a pure bat-missing lefty arm operating at elite efficiency levels on a brief but dominant A-ball sample. He's striking out 12.7 per 9 innings while walking just 1.6, putting him in the 99th percentile for both strikeout rate and K-BB% among the ValuCast pitcher pool. The hard flaw: this is 44.7 innings on A-ball, and when translated to MLB-equivalent rates his walk rate jumps to 2.7 per 9 while strikeouts fall to 8.5—a much tighter margin that raises questions about whether the command grades hold at higher competition. ValuCast is ranking him upward, but the sample is small and the level is low, so confidence in any ceiling projection remains guarded.

830402_pitcher.text: Kendry Chourio is a right-handed pitcher operating with elite control and strikeout suppression at A+, posting a 1.88 ERA and 0.92 WHIP across his best prior A-level sample (48 IP), while punching out 8.25 K/9 against just 1.69 BB/9. His current A+ run is too thin (4.7 IP) to trust; the jump in walk rate and ERA there signals he's still calibrating to the level, and his translated MLB equivalent K/9 of 7.4 sits below average for a starter. The read is a depth arm with modest strikeout stuff and legitimate command strength, but the small current sample and downward K rate in translation leave confidence low.

832562_pitcher.text: Dylan Brown is a left-handed pitcher operating as a bat-missing arm at A+, with a 13.2 K/9 that ranks 93rd percentile among the ValuCast pitcher pool and a K-BB% of 26.6% (97th percentile) that signals elite strikeout-to-walk separation. The main drag is run prevention—his 4.05 ERA and 1.38 WHIP (both around 61st percentile) show balls are finding play despite the impressive strikeout rate, a gap the translation model flags at higher uncertainty. The projection sees a multi-inning or setup arm ceiling over two to three years, though this is a modest 33.3 IP current sample with no stale-date risk.

834962_hitter.text: Anthony DePino is a power-over-hit hitter still learning the zone at 23, showing the thump—.504 SLG, .229 ISO at 89th percentile—but swinging through enough pitches (22.9% K) to keep him from running away with offensive impact. His walk rate sits at a respectable 13.4%, and the .886 OPS reflects a bat with real juice, though the strikeout volume tempers the consistency. The main risk is whether he can stay in the lineup without more contact; he projects as organizational depth with a bench-or-platoon ceiling (85% probability), needing to trim strikeouts and tighten his approach to climb higher. This is a fresh 157-PA sample, so the power is real but the hit tool remains unsettled enough to watch closely.

834978_pitcher.text: Danny Thompson Jr. is a right-handed pitcher showing plus strikeout stuff paired with walk management that trails his miss rate—a profile built on swing-and-miss with control that lags behind the swing-and-miss. In his A+ sample (47.3 IP), he struck out 12.93 per 9 while walking 4.56 per 9, a K-BB% of 21.9% that ranks 91st percentile among ValuCast's pitcher pool. The core risk is whether he can sustain that strikeout rate as competition tightens; his current AA sample is only 9 IP, making any read here thin and provisional. Floor is a depth arm, with modest probability of reaching useful depth relief value in the next one to two years.
